title: Unconventional superconductivity in locally non-centrosymmetric CeNi$_2$As$_2$
authors: Félix Morineau, Jan Knapp, Javier Landaeta, Thomas Lühmann, Lea Richter, Petra Knappova, Soumen Ash, Sushma Lakshmi Ravi Sankar, Konstantin Semeniuk, Elena Hassinger, Christoph Geibel, Manuel Brando, Daniel F. Agterberg, Andrew P. Mackenzie, Seunghyun Khim
abstract: Recent years have seen intense research on heavy fermion superconductivity, inspired by the discovery of multiple superconducting phases in UTe$_\text{2}$ and CeRh$_\text{2}$As$_\text{2}$. In the latter material, two superconducting phases observed under applied magnetic field oriented along the crystallographic $\textit{c}$ direction are associated with local inversion symmetry breaking. To advance understanding of these phenomena, it is highly desirable to find further examples of heavy fermion superconductivity in materials with locally non-centrosymmetric structure. We have succeeded in this quest, by growing single crystals of the CaBe$_\text{2}$Ge$_\text{2}$ isomorph of CeNi$_\text{2}$As$_\text{2}$. The resulting superconductivity brings more than we had foreseen. In addition to providing the opportunity to compare and contrast with that of CeRh$_\text{2}$As$_\text{2}$, the condensation occurs from an incoherent normal state quantitatively similar to that of UBe$_\text{13}$. Our findings therefore raise profound questions not just about superconductivity in the locally non-centrosymmetric structures, but about unconventional superconductivity itself.
summary: This work reports on superconductivity in $ eta$-CeNi$_2$As$_2$, a heavy fermion material with local structural asymmetry. The key finding is that the superconducting condensation occurs from an incoherent normal state, suggesting unconventional pairing mechanisms. By comparing its superconducting properties and upper critical fields to related compounds, the authors deepen the understanding of how symmetry and electronic correlations dictate pairing symmetry in strongly correlated systems.
main_problem: To find and understand heavy fermion superconductivity in materials exhibiting local inversion symmetry breaking, advancing the general understanding of unconventional superconductivity.
main_result: Superconductivity was confirmed in $ eta$-CeNi$_2$As$_2$ at $\approx 0.4$ K, which condenses from an incoherent normal state, raising profound questions about the pairing mechanism.
method: The study involved growing single crystals and performing comprehensive transport, thermodynamic (heat capacity), and magnetic susceptibility measurements under varying magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The research focuses on the $	ext{CaBe}_2	ext{Ge}_2$ isomorph of $	ext{CeNi}_2	ext{As}_2$, a heavy fermion superconductor with a locally non-centrosymmetric structure, comparing its behavior to $	ext{CeRh}_2	ext{As}_2$ and $	ext{UBe}_{13}$.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), electronic heat capacity coefficient ($\gamma$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), in-plane ($ho_{ab}$) and c-axis ($ho_c$) resistivity, and upper critical fields ($H_{c2}$).
important_parameters: Effective magnetic moment ($\approx 2.54 \mu_B$), characteristic energy scales ($\Delta_{	ext{CEF},1} \approx 10$ K), and critical fields relative to the Pauli limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed superconductivity is governed by the interplay between local non-centrosymmetry, heavy fermion behavior, and the nature of the normal state coherence.
figures_summary: Figures compare superconducting transition signatures (resistivity, $\chi$, $C/T$) and show unusual normal state behaviors, while other figures detail $H_{c2}$ anisotropy and phase diagrams comparing $ eta$-CeNi$_2$As$_2$ to CeRh$_2$As$_2$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the superconducting transition in the new material, characterizing the unusual normal state (incoherent/non-Fermi liquid), and finally probing the superconducting state using high-field measurements to constrain the pairing symmetry.
why_interesting: The investigation into superconductivity arising from an incoherent normal state, far from a Fermi liquid, challenges standard BCS theory and connects structural symmetry breaking (Rashba SOC) to pairing symmetry, which is a key area in strongly correlated electron physics.

The major difference lies in the coordination of the constituting Ni-As layer that separates the Ce layer. α- CeNi2As2 has Ni coordinated at the tetrahedral site surrounded with As while in β-CeNi2As2 one of the Ni-As layers has a complete interchange of the Ni and As positions. c, Powder x-ray diffraction pattern on crushed single-crystalline sample agrees with the expected pattern (d) for β-CeNi2As2 but clearly departs from the one for α-CeNi2As2. Detailed crystal structures are presented in Extended Data Tables A2-A4.
